## Storage and lifecycle

`src/games.rs` initializes additive SQLite tables alongside the existing quiz
schema. Every **Start a game** creates a cryptographically random, unambiguous
join code and a new `games` row. In one transaction it snapshots the quiz title
and only active questions/options, in their preparation order. Snapshot IDs,
players, and answers are game-specific. Import/export still transfers only quiz
contents; it never transfers games or player identities.

The persistent state machine is:

```
waiting --Start--> open --Finish--> closed --Next--> open …
                                      └--End quiz--> ended (last question only)
```

An empty snapshot goes directly from waiting to ended on Start. A version number
increments with every phase transition and prize-selection command. Moderator commands include the version
rendered in their browser; stale/double requests return 409 with fresh state, not
another transition. The SQLite mutex serializes Finish with answering, so an
answer either commits before closure or is rejected. Each (question, player)
has one answer, updated atomically on a new pick. The phone serializes requests
and coalesces rapid taps so the last user intent is the last submitted pick.
A per-answer revision prevents a delayed response from undoing newer UI state.

Quiz editing cannot affect a snapshot. Deleting a preparation quiz unlinks, but
does not destroy, its games. Game state, names, identity tokens, and answers
survive restarts. The transient presence cache is rebuilt as phones reconnect.
The quiz page lists its games, newest first, with an Open game link in each item.

## Routes and authorization

- `POST /moderate/quizzes/{id}/games`: create and redirect to the big screen.
- `/moderate/games/{code}`: big screen; `/state`, `/events`, `/control`, and
  `/qr.svg` below it are also protected by the existing Basic auth middleware.
- `GET /play/{code}`: public join/phone page. POST joins (JSON for the JS client,
  or a redirect for an ordinary form). `/state` and `/events` below it provide
  role-filtered state; `/answer` and `/presence` accept player POSTs.

only to `/play/{code}`, with a one-year lifetime. Tokens are scoped again by game
in every database lookup. A second tab or reopening the join URL restores that
player; a cookie from another game is not accepted. Mutations require HMAC CSRF
tokens tied to the game and identity. Joining after end creates no player.

Player and moderator JSON use dedicated view types, never serialization of the
quiz preparation structs. Open questions contain option ID/text only: no
`correct`, `count`, `result`, future question, or answer-key fields. Closed
questions add correctness, and moderator views add historical per-option counts.
Players receive only their own name/selection/result and cannot read anyone
else's answers. Anonymous visitors only receive the join/end state. All state
and game HTML is no-store. Host names are unrestricted; the HTTP join URL and
QR payload are constructed from the same request Host. QR SVG generation is
local (`qrcode` crate), with no web service or remote resources.

comments. Each game has separate watch channels for moderator updates, phase

answer fan-out. Watch channels coalesce bursts and never accumulate an unbounded
queue for a slow phone. A fresh, role-filtered snapshot is read after subscribing
and on every notification, so reconnects need no historical event replay.
